samples.summary: Text-box `stepSelectionFontSize` still reads raw `inline.style.fontSize`, now inconsistent with the summary that drives the picker
samples.evidence: `getRangeStyleSummary` in the text-box editor was switched to `visitStyledRunsInRange`, which layers named-style inline defaults (`resolveStyleInline`) under each run (packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts:56). The frontend font-size picker takes its value straight from that summary (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/use-resolved-font-size.ts:40). But the co-located stepper was left untouched: packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:887 still computes `const size = inline.style.fontSize ?? DEFAULT_INLINE_STYLE.fontSize ?? 11`. So for a text-box/slides block whose named style supplies the size (e.g. a heading block — slides renders it through docs `computeLayout`, which applies BUILTIN_STYLES, packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:150), the picker now shows 20 while pressing `+` steps 11→12, making the displayed size jump downward. The docs editor's own stepper was already effective-style aware (editor.ts:1110), so only the text-box path is now out of sync. Fix belongs in text-box-editor.ts's `collectRunsInBlock` (switch it to `visitStyledRunsInRange` too).

samples.summary: Text-box collapsed-caret summary path still returns raw run style, so the #715 keyboard/toolbar disagreement survives for carets in styled blocks
samples.evidence: The change makes `TextEditor.toggleStyle` decide from `styleDefaultsAtCursor()` + visual style for a collapsed caret (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2898/3006), and makes the range branch of the text-box summary effective-style aware. The collapsed branch of the text-box summary was not updated: packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1035 returns `{ ...inline.style, ...staged }` with no `resolveStyleInline` layer (compare the docs editor, which does layer defaults at editor.ts:2712-2722). Consequence in a slides/docs text box whose block's named style supplies italic: the toolbar's Italic toggle reads `undefined` → applies `italic: true` → pending style with no visual change (a permanent no-op, the exact #715 shape), while Cmd+I on the same caret now correctly writes `italic: false`. The toolbar `pressed` state also disagrees with the keyboard for the same caret.

samples.summary: `stepSelectionFontSize` now resizes every cell of a table caught inside a cross-block selection (new behaviour for an exported API)
samples.evidence: `visitStyledRunsInRange` reads a table block whole when it falls inside a cross-block selection (packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts:171-176) and normalizes cell endpoints to the parent table (range-runs.ts:150-155). The old collector in stepSelectionFontSize skipped table blocks (blockLen of a table block is 0) and bailed out entirely when an endpoint sat in a cell. The frontend font-size +/- buttons (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-size-picker usage via `stepSelectionFontSize`) therefore now rewrite the font size of every cell of any table crossed by the selection, and the picker will read 'mixed' (→ empty box, use-resolved-font-size.ts:39) where it previously showed a value. Consistent with `Doc.applyInlineStyle` and probably intended, but it is a user-visible behaviour change to an exported API beyond the B/I/U fix the change advertises.

samples.summary: Shared walk resolves named-style overrides from `doc.document.styles`, but the text-box renderer lays out with `docStyles` undefined
samples.evidence: range-runs.ts:56 uses `resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), doc.document.styles)`, while the text-box editor's layout passes `undefined` for `docStyles` (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:462-469; `computeLayout`'s 7th parameter is `docStyles`, layout.ts:368). If a text-box document ever carries a `styles` override registry, the summary (and now the keyboard toggle verdict) would report values the text-box renderer never paints — the same read/write divergence this change set out to remove. Built-in definitions are unaffected because `resolveStyleInline(id, undefined)` still returns `BUILTIN_STYLES[id].inline`. To confirm, I would need a text-box/slides document that populates `document.styles`.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The change made TextEditor.toggleStyle decide add-vs-remove from named-style defaults layered under the caret style (text-editor.ts:2898 + styleDefaultsAtCursor at 3006-3010), and updated the docs editor's collapsed summary to match (editor.ts:2707-2723 returns { ...defaults, ...inline.style }). The text-box editor's collapsed branch was NOT updated: text-box-editor.ts:1035 (and getSelectionStyle at 1010) still returns raw `{ ...inline.style, ...staged }`, while its range branch does layer defaults via visitStyledRunsInRange (text-box-editor.ts:1076 -> range-runs.ts:56). A styled block inside a text box is reachable: setBlockType accepts 'heading' with any level (text-box-editor.ts:1146-1156 rejects only title/subtitle/hr/table/page-break) and the shared TextEditor keyboard path Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+1..6 converts the caret block to a heading (text-editor.ts:1028-1041); heading-6's built-in style supplies italic:true (named-styles.ts:91) and text-box layout applies built-ins even with docStyles undefined (text-box-editor.ts:462 -> layout.ts:149-157, named-styles.ts:119-127). The broken consumer is the toolbar, which reads both `pressed` and the toggle direction from getRangeStyleSummary (frontend text-format-group.tsx:96,106,181) and is wired to the slides text-box editor (slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:445). So for a collapsed caret the toolbar reads italic undefined while Cmd+I computes italic:false — the #715 keyboard/toolbar disagreement, in a consumer the diff did not update. This is a changed-contract-with-unupdated-consumer finding, squarely in the blast-radius lane; major impact.

finding.summary: New shared read walk recurses into nested tables; the write path (`Doc.applyInlineStyle`) does not — reintroducing the read/write divergence this module exists to remove
finding.evidence: `visitStyledRunsInRange`'s `visitTable` recurses when a cell block is itself a table (packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts:75-79). The write it claims to mirror does not: `Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s table branch loops rows/cells and calls `store.applyStyle(cellBlock.id, 0, len, ...)` with `len = getBlockTextLength(cellBlock)`, which is 0 for a nested table block, so nested-table content is never styled (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:415-429). Nested tables are a supported docs feature (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:475, packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:136). Consequence for a cross-block selection containing a table that contains a nested table: the read sees the nested runs (unstyled) so `isStyleOnInSelection` / the summary answer "not all on" forever, the write styles only the outer runs, and Cmd+B / the toolbar button can never remove bold again — the exact #715 shape.

verdict.reason: The finding's core factual claim — that `visitStyledRunsInRange`'s `visitTable` recurses into nested tables — is not present in the code. `visitTable` (packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts:78-94) calls only `visitWholeBlock(cellBlock)`; there is no recursive `visitTable` call anywhere in the file (its sole call site is line 176), and an explicit comment at lines 84-90 states the non-recursion is deliberate for exactly the reason the reviewer worries about. The cited evidence range (lines 75-79) contains `visitWholeBlock`'s definition and `visitTable`'s `if (!block.tableData) return;`, not recursion. Read and write are in fact identical for nested tables: read does `visitBlockSlice(id, 0, getBlockTextLength(block))` (range-runs.ts:75-76), and `getBlockTextLength` sums inline text lengths (model/types.ts:326-328) which is 0 for table blocks since they are built with `inlines: []` (model/types.ts:529-533, import/docx-importer.ts:491-496), so the overlap test `inlineEnd > from && pos < to` never fires — a no-op. The write path (model/document.ts:415-429) likewise guards `if (len > 0)` and skips nested-table blocks. Both paths cover exactly the same run set, so the alleged read/write divergence and the resulting 'can never remove bold' trap cannot occur via this mechanism.

finding.summary: `stepSelectionFontSize` still carries the old duplicated walk, breaking the documented invariant that it uses the same traversal as `getRangeStyleSummary`
finding.evidence: `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl` keeps the pre-change dispatch, including the body-only `layout.blockParentMap` lookup the diff's own comment calls unable to resolve header/footer cells (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1163-1164) and no cell→table normalization for cross-block ranges. Its doc comment asserts "the same block/offset dispatch `getRangeStyleSummary` uses" (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1080-1082), and docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:213 repeats it — both are now false because the summary moved to `visitStyledRunsInRange` (doc.blockParentMap, table normalization, table recursion). Observable: for a multi-block selection inside a header/footer table cell the size picker now reads a real value/'mixed' while the ± stepper collects zero runs and silently does nothing; for a selection spanning a body table the summary reports the table's sizes as 'mixed' but the stepper never touches them.

verdict.reason:
The claimed code does not exist. `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl` does NOT keep a duplicated pre-change dispatch: its run-collection pass is a single call to the shared walk — `visitStyledRunsInRange(doc, range, (effective, _inline, block, from, to) => { ... runs.push(...) })` at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1110-1113 — which is exactly the same helper `getRangeStyleSummary` uses at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2769. So the doc comment at editor.ts:1081-1086 and docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:210-215 are accurate, not false.

The evidence cited as the "body-only `layout.blockParentMap` lookup" at editor.ts:1163-1164 is misquoted: those lines are inside `notifyStyleApplied()` and contain `anchor/focus/tableCellRange` field copies, no `blockParentMap` access at all. The only `layout.blockParentMap` reference inside the stepper is editor.ts:1140-1141, used solely to pick a top-level id to `markDirty` for repaint after the styles were already applied — it does not gate which runs are collected or styled.

Header/footer and cross-block cell→table normalization are handled inside the shared walk, not in the stepper: packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts:123-126 resolves endpoints through the merged `doc.blockParentMap` (body + header + footer), range-runs.ts:155 normalizes cell endpoints to their parent table for top-level cross-block ranges, and range-runs.ts:175 recurses into table blocks. Therefore both claimed observables ("stepper collects zero runs and silently does nothing" for header/footer cell selections; "stepper never touches" body-table runs the summary reports) are refuted by construction — both entry points traverse identical code.

finding.summary: Text-box editors (docs text boxes, slides shape/text-box text) now have a keyboard-vs-toolbar disagreement: the shared keyboard walk layers named-style defaults, their own `getRangeStyleSummary` does not
finding.evidence: `TextEditor` is also instantiated by the docs text-box editor (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:666), which slides wraps (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:109, 601-602). The new `isStyleOnInSelection` reads effective styles including `resolveStyleInline` defaults (packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts:52), but the text-box summary the toolbars read walks raw `inline.style` only, with no defaults layered (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1067-1088). Heading 6's built-in style sets `italic: true` (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:91), so on a heading-6 block in a text box Cmd+I now writes `italic:false` while `TextFormatGroup`/mobile-toolbar show the button unpressed and apply `italic:true` — the same class of read disagreement the change set out to remove. The task note claims both editors resolve defaults identically (docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:31-34), which is not true of the text-box implementation.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim is not present in the repository. The docs text-box editor's `getRangeStyleSummary` range branch does NOT walk raw `inline.style`: it imports and calls the same shared walk as the keyboard path — `visitStyledRunsInRange(doc, range, (effective) => ...)` at packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1076 (import at :37), consuming the `effective` style. That walk layers named-style inline defaults under each run (packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts:56 and :63), which is exactly what `TextEditor.isStyleOnInSelection` consumes (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3035) and what the full docs editor's summary consumes (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2769). Therefore a heading-6 block in a text box reads `italic: true` in both the toolbar summary and the keyboard toggle; the claimed Cmd+I-writes-false / toolbar-shows-unpressed divergence cannot arise on the cited path, and the Slides wrapper (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:601-602) merely delegates to that same implementation. The task note at docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:31-34 refers to the collapsed-caret path matching `getSelectionStyle()`, which is true within the text-box editor (text-box-editor.ts:1000-1015 vs 1024-1041). The only real residual — the text-box collapsed-caret branch not layering defaults the way editor.ts:2707-2723 does — is a different mechanism than the one asserted, is self-corrected by the staged pending merge, and is at most a minor cosmetic pressed-state inconsistency, not the major contract divergence claimed.
